_note: Short self-check per domain. Adapted from the original SEC+ // ACADEMY scenario questions: rewritten with plausible distractors, objective numbers checked against SY0-701. Practice only, not a predictor of exam results.

questions.q: A team installs a camera so unauthorized entry can be identified and reviewed afterward. What is the camera's main function?
questions.why: It records and identifies an event rather than stopping it, so its main job is detective. (A visible camera can also deter, but that is a secondary effect.)

questions.q: A legacy app cannot support MFA, so the team puts it behind a jump host and adds extra monitoring. What kind of control is this?
questions.why: When the preferred control cannot be used, an alternative that reduces the same risk is a compensating control.

questions.q: An employee signs in successfully but is blocked from opening payroll records. Which step blocked them?
questions.why: Authentication already proved who they are. Authorization decides what they are allowed to do, and payroll was not on the list.

questions.q: A production firewall change is approved, but nobody has written down how to undo it if it breaks things. What is missing?
questions.why: A backout or rollback plan is the documented way to safely reverse a change that goes wrong.

questions.q: You want to confirm a downloaded installer was not altered. What is the most direct way?
options: Compare its hash to the publisher's published hash
questions.why: Hashes detect changes. Get the expected hash from a trusted source and compare it with the hash of your copy.

questions.q: A well-funded group quietly copies a company's proprietary research over many months. What is the most likely motivation?
questions.why: Long, quiet, targeted theft of strategic information points to espionage, often by an APT or nation-state group.

questions.q: A trusted vendor ships a software update that contains malicious code. Which threat vector is this?
questions.why: The malware reached victims through a trusted supplier's product, which makes it a supply chain attack.

questions.q: An app builds database queries by pasting raw user input into the SQL text. What is the best fix?
options: Add a CAPTCHA to the form
questions.why: Parameterized queries keep user input as data so it can never change the structure of the SQL command. The other options do not fix the root cause.

questions.q: One workstation contacts the same unfamiliar external IP every 60 seconds, around the clock. What pattern is this?
questions.why: Regular, repeated check-ins to an outside host are a classic sign of command-and-control beaconing.

questions.q: An unsupported legacy device cannot be patched. What most directly limits an attacker's ability to move from it to other systems?
questions.why: Segmentation controls which systems the device can talk to, which limits lateral movement even when the device itself stays vulnerable.

questions.q: A company runs its own operating system on a cloud virtual machine (IaaS). Who usually patches that guest OS?
questions.why: In IaaS, the provider runs the physical hardware and virtualization layer. The customer manages the guest OS and everything on it.

questions.q: Where should a public-facing web server usually go?
options: In the same segment as the domain controllers
questions.why: A screened subnet separates internet-facing systems from sensitive internal networks, with tightly limited traffic between them.

questions.q: A sensitive field is replaced with a stand-in value, and the real value can only be looked up in a protected vault. What is this called?
questions.why: Tokenization swaps the real value for a token and keeps the mapping somewhere protected. Masking just hides part of the value on display.

questions.q: A system has an RPO of 10 minutes. What does that number describe?
options: The most data (in time) you can afford to lose
questions.why: RPO is about data loss measured in time. RTO is about how long recovery takes.

questions.q: You need backups that copy only what changed since the last FULL backup. Which type is that?
questions.why: Differential backups copy everything changed since the last full backup. Incremental backups copy changes since the last backup of any type.

questions.q: A laptop is stolen while powered off. What best protects the files stored on it?
questions.why: Full-disk encryption keeps data at rest unreadable without the key. The other tools mostly help while the system is running.

questions.q: What is the most reliable way to find servers nobody is managing?
options: Reconcile the asset inventory against network discovery
questions.why: You can't secure what you don't know about. Comparing the inventory with what is actually on the network turns up unknown or orphaned systems.

questions.q: After patching a critical vulnerability, what confirms the fix actually worked?
options: Rescanning or otherwise validating the system
questions.why: A rescan or other validation checks that the original weakness is really gone.

questions.q: Which tool most directly correlates sign-in events and network events from many sources?
questions.why: A SIEM gathers logs from many sources and correlates them, so related events show up together.

questions.q: A domain owner wants receiving mail servers to reject messages that fail SPF/DKIM alignment. Which record does that?
questions.why: DMARC tells receivers how to handle mail that fails aligned SPF or DKIM checks, and where to send reports.

questions.q: Access depends on the user's department AND whether their device is compliant. Which access model fits best?
questions.why: Attribute-based access control looks at attributes of the user, the resource, and the context (like device health) to make each decision.

questions.q: An automated workflow is about to disable hundreds of accounts after one noisy alert. What is the best safeguard?
options: An approval gate and limits on scope
Giving the workflow global admin rights
questions.why: High-impact automated actions need guardrails: human approval, limits on how much they can change, and logging.

questions.q: The team isolates infected machines to stop the spread. Which incident response phase is this?
questions.why: Containment limits ongoing damage. Eradication (removing the cause) and recovery come after.

questions.q: You need a list of which internal hosts talked to an external IP, without full packet contents. What is the best source?
questions.why: Flow data records who talked to whom, on which ports, and how much, without storing payloads. Packet capture works but is heavier than you need.

questions.q: Which document usually gives step-by-step instructions for following a policy?
questions.why: Policies set the rule, standards set required specifics, guidelines suggest, and procedures give the steps.

questions.q: A loss event costs $20,000 each time and is expected 0.5 times per year. What is the ALE?
A new supplier will store your employee data. What should happen first?
options: Security due diligence and contract terms
Grant access now and review later
Send the data encrypted, then sign the contract
Rely on the supplier's marketing materials
questions.why: Assess the vendor and agree on contract terms (notification, right to audit, data handling) before sharing sensitive data.

questions.q: A company wants to reduce its privacy exposure. Which practice fits best?
questions.why: Collecting and keeping only the personal data you actually need reduces what can be exposed.

questions.q: An authorized test actually exploits weaknesses to show what an attacker could do. What is it?
questions.why: A penetration test tries controlled exploitation. A vulnerability scan only finds and ranks weaknesses.

questions.q: Besides course completion rates, what best shows a phishing-awareness program is working?
options: More people reporting suspicious messages, and reporting faster
questions.why: Behavior is the real measure. More reports, faster, and fewer repeat clicks show the training is changing what people do.
